summary: Verified the targeted bug fix for setup -> dashboard transition (App.js setup-status race + SetupWizard finish + TelemetryService submitSetup timeout). All three scenarios PASS end-to-end via Playwright on the public preview URL (mobile 390x844, dm_device_id seeded via addInitScript BEFORE goto). (1) FRESH-INSTALL FLOW: brand-new device_id -> Launch App -> setup-wizard visible -> filled all 6 steps with Playwright .fill() (Cain / acc11 / rec22 / wip33 / 'find my phone' / +15551234567) -> setup-finish -> within ~1s the dashboard (data-testid security-dashboard + live-monitor) appeared, setup-wizard gone, cover NOT shown, app-loading NOT shown. Critically, after waiting +5s extra (long enough for any stale setupStatus() promise to resolve), the wizard STILL did NOT reappear and the dashboard STILL visible — confirming the cancel-flag + functional updater (prev===null ? !!s.configured : prev) prevents the late status response from overwriting configured=true. (2) VALIDATION: mismatched access codes on step1 blocked with toast 'Access codes do not match' (stayed on step1); duplicate wipe==access on step3 blocked with toast 'Wipe code must be unique' (stayed on step3); empty trusted number on finish blocked with toast 'Add at least one trusted number' (stayed on step5, dashboard NOT shown). (3) REFRESH/COVER REMEMBERS SETUP: pre-configured TEST_dm_cover_1781238535_25225 via POST /api/security/setup with numeric access_code=2580 (returned {ok:true,configured:true}); seeded same dm_device_id; reload -> Launch App -> cover-calculator shown (setup-wizard NOT shown) -> tapped calc-key 2,5,8,0,equals -> security-dashboard + live-monitor appeared. Backend regression: POST /api/security/setup still returns 200 {ok:true,configured:true,cover_app:calculator} for the wizard payload and GET /setup/status returns persisted profile/trusted_numbers. Bug fix is fully verified — no regressions found.
critical_code_review_comments: App.js setup-status fix is correct: cancel flag + functional updater (prev===null?...:prev) guarantees a late telemetry.setupStatus() resolution can never flip configured back to false after onDone has set it to true. Consider also clearing the in-flight request explicitly via AbortController so the network request itself is cancelled (minor — current cancel flag is sufficient to prevent the state bug).

SetupWizard.finish() correctly resets busy via setBusy(false) in the same flow (outside try/catch) so a thrown error no longer leaves the button stuck on 'Saving…'. The 20s axios timeout in TelemetryService.submitSetup is a good defensive backstop.

Minor: onDone in App.js sets BOTH configured=true and unlocked=true, so the freshly-set-up owner skips the cover screen and goes straight to the dashboard. That matches the screenshot/test expectations but is worth documenting — a fresh-setup user is implicitly trusted and never has to enter the access code they just chose. If the product wants 'first-time access verification', onDone should set configured=true but leave unlocked=false so the cover-calculator demands the access code once before the first dashboard view.

SetupWizard step 1 currently accepts alphanumeric access codes (e.g. 'acc11'), but the Calculator cover only accepts digits — so an owner who chose an alphanumeric access code on first install can NEVER unlock the device via the calculator cover after a refresh. Either constrain the access-code input to digits (inputMode='numeric' + pattern=[0-9]+) or change the cover to accept letters too. This is a real foot-gun (the wizard happily saved 'acc11' but the cover can't type it).

App.js useEffect that calls telemetry.setupStatus() depends only on [screen]; if a user toggles screen state rapidly during the initial render, multiple in-flight status calls could compete. The cancel flag handles this for the most recent effect, but earlier effects' promises still settle and are silently dropped — fine here but worth noting.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (3/3 scenarios passed: fresh-install -> dashboard; validation blocks + toasts; refresh remembers setup -> cover -> unlock -> dashboard)

context_for_next_testing_agent: The setup -> dashboard transition bug is FIXED and verified. Key observations for future iterations: (a) when scripting Playwright for this app, ALWAYS use addInitScript to seed dm_device_id BEFORE page.goto (mid-session injection is racy and will desync the harness). (b) The 'Launch App' button has no data-testid; use page.get_by_text('Try the Demo') as a more reliable entry. (c) Setup wizard accepts alphanumeric codes but the Calculator cover only accepts digits — if a future test reloads after wizard setup with alphanumeric codes it will be unable to unlock; use numeric codes via the API for cover tests. (d) After setup-finish the app sets BOTH configured=true and unlocked=true, so fresh-install users go straight to the dashboard without the cover screen. (e) The +5s post-finish wait is the critical assertion that proves the stale-status-response race is fixed.
rca of the issue: Original bug: App.js had a useEffect on [screen] that called telemetry.setupStatus().then(s => setConfigured(!!s.configured)). If the user finished the wizard before that promise resolved, onDone set configured=true then the late .then() callback unconditionally overwrote it back to false (or true again later), causing the SetupWizard to remount at step 0 and lose its state — appearing as 'wizard reset' or stuck on 'Saving…'. Fix applied in App.js: setConfigured((prev) => (prev === null ? !!(s && s.configured) : prev)) — the late response is only allowed to write when configured is still null (initial check). A cancel flag (let cancelled = false; return () => { cancelled = true; }) also bails out before calling setState if the effect has been torn down. Defence-in-depth: TelemetryService.submitSetup now has a 20s axios timeout so submitSetup can never hang silently; SetupWizard.finish() wraps the submit in try/catch with toast.error + setBusy(false) so the user always gets feedback and the button never stays in 'Saving…' forever. Verified: dashboard appears within ~1s of finish and persists through a +5s wait that would have previously caught the stale resolution. No further action required.
